summary: As of November 18, 2026, junk-bond spreads are 3.47 percentage points and are up 0.17 percentage points over five trading days. Investment-grade spreads are up 0.03 percentage points over those same five trading days. The CCC-minus-BB gap is 11.48 percentage points. Of the 0.22 percentage-point move in the all-in junk yield, 0.17 was the credit spread and 0.05 was Treasury rates. The 10-year yield is 5.07 percent as of November 18, 2026 and the 30-year is 5.41 percent as of November 18, 2026, a gap of 0.34 percentage points. Brent is 89.97 dollars a barrel as of November 19, 2026 (-6.11 percent over five trading days), and the curve is backwardation. The 5-year inflation breakeven is 2.22 percent as of November 19, 2026, down 0.09 percentage points over five observations. The 10-year real yield is 2.88 percent as of November 18, 2026. The broad dollar index is 122.65 as of November 13, 2026, +1.08 index points over 20 observations. VIX is 24.56 as of November 18, 2026. The Fed balance sheet is 6.74 trillion dollars as of November 18, 2026, down 12 billion dollars over the latest four weekly observations. Reserve balances are 2.98 trillion dollars as of November 18, 2026, up 17 billion dollars over the latest four weekly observations. Overnight reverse repo is 0.405 billion dollars as of November 19, 2026, up 0.08 billion over the latest four observations.
